newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disappointed at EU move on Helms-Burton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disappointed at EU move on Helms-Burton.

text.p: The United States expressed disappointment at a decision by the European Union on Tuesday to proceed with a complaint to the World Trade Organisation against Washington's anti-Cuba laws.
"We think this is most unfortunate," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters. "We are disappointed at this."

EU foreign ministers, meeting in Luxembourg, unexpectedly decided not to wait to file the complaint and agreed to challenge the United States on its controversial Helms-Burton Act at the WTO in Geneva.

"We would have vastly preferred a bilateral, if you will, EU-U.S. solution to this and continued dialogue," Burns said adding that the United States had sent envoy Stuart Eizenstat "in good faith" to talk to European countries about it. "We believe that Helms-Burton should continue to be discussed between friends and that unilateral action should not be taken," he said.

Under Helms-Burton, passed in July, Washington has banned from the United States top executives of foreign companies considered to have profited from property confiscated from naturalised Americans by Cuba's communist government.
"The Europeans ought to be concerned about human rights in Cuba and democracy in Cuba. They ought to be more concerned than they appear to be about those issues," Burns said.
